- Model consistently underestimates prices, especially in early days of the forecast horizon (e.g., first 5–10 days).
- Overestimates prices after sharp spikes in recent history (e.g., after 70.93–72.65 peaks, model overshoots by 1–3 points).
- Shows persistent lag in capturing true price reversals — tends to delay downward corrections after peaks.
- Mean reversion bias: model overreacts to short-term volatility, underestimating long-term trend toward mid-range values.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are overly pessimistic in the first 10 days, then gradually adjust — but often still too low by end of horizon.
- Avoids “noise” in early data — ignores minor fluctuations in first 5–7 days, leading to underestimation of volatility.
